dossier_meta.subject: Graph Theory
dossier_meta.statement_text: Conjecture Every simple graph on five or more vertices is switching-reconstructible.
dossier_meta.context_text: To switch a vertex of a simple graph is to exchange its sets of neighbours and non-neighbours. The graph so obtained is called a switching of the graph. The collection of switchings of a graph G is called the switching deck of $ G $ . A graph is switching-reconstructible if every graph with the same deck as $ G $ is isomorphic to $ G $ . There are four pairs of non-isomorphic graphs of order $ 4 $ with the same switching deck. One of them consists of the empty graph and the $ 4 $ -cycle. Stanley [S] proved that a graph on $ n $ vertices is switching-reconstructible if $ n \not\equiv 0 (\mod 4) $ . An analogous problem was posed for digraphs. Instead of complementing the edges at a vertex, one reverses each of its incident arc.
dossier_meta.references_text: - *[S] R. P. Stanley Reconstruction from vertex-switching. J. Combin. Theory Ser. B, 38 (1985), 132--138.
